look_here_first: ROUGH DROPSEED (perennial): begin with its very narrow, contracted upright panicle, then confirm a persistent basal crown. Against S. compositus, compare mature spikelet/lemma microtexture and fresh-grain pericarp response rather than plant height or panicle outline alone; against annual S. vaginiflorus, examine the rooted base and narrow leaf-sheath heads.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora; Travis and Williamson — county distribution layer explicitly records both counties.

best_field_traits: ligule a very short fringe of hairs
crew_field_check: Perennial dropseed with a tight, slender panicle; can closely resemble composite dropseed. Narrowness is a field clue, not proof. True discriminators include glume-to-lemma proportions and mature grain pericarp (typically NOT gelatinizing/slipping off the seed when freshly wetted); lemma prickle features need a compound microscope for confident scoring.
1-flowered, awnless Sporobolus spikelets — not the multi-flowered bristled clusters of Setaria/Cenchrus.
Photographs of head outline are first clues, NOT confirmed lemma/pericarp identification.
Anther/flower color, panicle width and small/large height alone are not safe identifications.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Gather mature grains and intact glume/lemma, not just plant silhouette.
field_matrix.difference: Both perennial; S. compositus pericarp typically gelatinizes and separates when wetted, unlike S. clandestinus. Panicle form overlaps and varieties complicate appearance.
field_matrix.guardrail: Fresh mature seed is needed: older stored seed may react slowly or poorly; use multiple characters.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Check basal roots and crown, panicle and concealed upper-sheath spikelets.
field_matrix.difference: Typically a much shorter annual with terminal and axillary panicles; annual versus perennial is helpful on a rooted adult, not always clear in a drought-stunted plant.
field_matrix.guardrail: Concealed sheath spikelets are not exclusive to poverty dropseed in this section.

not_reliable_alone: Presence of hidden sheath flowers (multiple related dropseeds can have these)
Being taller/shorter or open/contracted at a single drought-stressed moment
Claiming a micro-lemma character from an ordinary phone photograph

field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: Perennial dropseed with a tight, slender panicle; can closely resemble composite dropseed. Narrowness is a field clue, not proof. True discriminators include glume-to-lemma proportions and mature grain pericarp (typically NOT gelatinizing/slipping off the seed when freshly wetted); lemma prickle features need a compound microscope for confident scoring.
photo_targets: Intact rooted base with persistent perennial crown
Whole contracted flowering and mature seedheads with ruler
Detached mature glume/lemma at 10–20× with glume-to-lemma dimensions
Mature grain photographed dry and after measured water interval; no ID based on aged grains alone
For exact microtexture, compound microscope view (~400×) of lemma surface, never fake 10× features
field_id_finish_pass.photo_limit: Current images show only gross structures; no verified upper-sheath concealed flower, glume-to-lemma measurement or lemma micromorphology. No original source determinations changed.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Dropseed — what can this photograph really identify?
steps: Check whether the photographed plant includes a ROOTED base: annual or perennial is NOT proven by an unrooted picture.
Follow the flowering axis into a true one-flowered dropseed spikelet. These panicles can look similar across species.
Search the upper leaf SHEATH for enclosed axillary flowers, but do not use this as an exclusive S. vaginiflorus test.
Measure fresh mature spikelets and inspect the lemma; compare fresh grain pericarp only if separating the S. compositus complex.
If no mature flowers, true crown or measured seed characters, identify only Sporobolus sp. or tentative complex.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use visible macro morphology first and defer difficult perennial-species separations to mature material, reliable grain tests and microscope when necessary.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Do not mistake labels and source IDs for independently confirmed Hays vouchers; exact microscope and concealed flower photographs remain missing.
